# Corpus Mining: Sam Reifler, *I Ching: A New Interpretation for Modern Times* (Bantam 1974)

Source: `/mnt/agents/upload/_OceanofPDF.com_I_Ching_A_New_Interpretation_for_Modern_Times_-_Sam_Reifler.pdf` (292 pp., scanned; extracted via `pdftotext -layout`; the trigram attribute table at book pp. 14–15 is a rotated image recovered via OCR). Page numbers below are the book's printed page numbers.

**Book's core project:** keep the traditional meanings of the hexagrams but rewrite the *language* for a modern (1970s counter-culture) reader: "In interpreting the I Ching anew I have not changed the meanings of the hexagrams, but have changed the language of the interpretations so that they speak to you and me" (Intro, ~p. 7).

---

## 1. SMALLEST FRAGMENTS (decomposition)

### 1.1 Line types (4 primitive tokens)
Numeric generation, yarrow and coin (pp. 8–10):
- **6 = moving Yin line** ("Old Yin", drawn —x—) — changes to Yang
- **7 = Yang line** (static, solid)
- **8 = Yin line** (static, broken)
- **9 = moving Yang line** ("Old Yang", drawn —o—) — changes to Yin

Yarrow ritual (50 sticks, pp. 8–9): remove 1, split bundle, count off by fours, three reduction rounds → remainder piles of 9/5, then 8/4, then 8/4. Pile of 9 or 8 = value **2**; pile of 5 or 4 = value **3**. Sum of three pile values ∈ {6,7,8,9} gives the line.
Coin oracle (p. 10): three coins; inscribed side/tails = 2, blank side/heads = 3; six tosses, bottom to top.

"The principle behind the I Ching is change: the inevitable change of a Yin force into a Yang force and vice versa. These changes are represented by the moving lines: the 6 line — Old Yin; the 9 line — Old Yang" (p. 11).

### 1.2 Yin/Yang as ur-polarity
- Broken line = Yin, solid line = Yang, "composed in a vertical pattern of six" (Intro, p. 4).
- Yin/Yang "only roughly correspond to the Western duality of feminine and masculine" (p. 4).
- Hexagram 2 gloss: "Yang represents the powers that direct and impel action. Yin represents action directly" (p. 23) — note this inverts the usual active/passive assignment. [noteworthy primitive]

### 1.3 Evolutionary stacking of the figure (p. 13)
- 1 line: Yes / No oracle.
- 2 lines: "Yes, but…" / "No, but…".
- 3 lines: the 8 trigrams, each with a name and attributes.
- 6 lines: hexagram = "a pair of trigrams"; meaning "derives from the qualities of its trigrams and their related positions" (p. 13).

### 1.4 The 8 trigrams (Reifler's names, p. 13)
Heaven · Earth · Thunder · The Deep/Water · Mountain · Wind/Wood · Fire/Sun · The Marsh/Mist.

### 1.5 Inner (nuclear) trigrams
"The ancient interpreters also took into account a second pair of trigrams, the intertwining 'inner trigrams' formed by lines 2, 3, and 4 and lines 3, 4, and 5 of the hexagrams" (p. 16, footnote refers to Wilhelm).

### 1.6 Hexagram as unit
- 64 hexagrams = "sixty-four examples of different ways of life, ways of being that covered the entire range of human experience" (Intro, ~pp. 4–5). "Sixty-four was found to be the most convenient number. (The mathematics of the system requires a square number.)"
- Hexagrams "are not determined by the counting off of sticks or the falling of coins, but are determined by the forces of Yin and Yang within the individual" (Intro, p. 4).
- A cast hexagram = "his Tao, his natural direction, in the case of the particular problem" (Intro, ~p. 5).

### 1.7 Idiosyncratic primitives Reifler invents
1. **artha / kama / moksha** — every hexagram interpretation is split into three sections "making liberal and inexact use of the names of three Hindu principles" (p. 12):
   - *artha* = relationship to other people, authorities, things; practical life, courses of action in society.
   - *kama* = love relationships (sexual, familial, close friends).
   - *moksha* = spiritual path; "indicates the proper spiritual path for the questioner at this juncture and also may reveal blocks and inconsistencies in his present philosophical position."
2. **"Friend"** — a postulated gender-neutral character representing the other person in the kama section (p. 12).
3. **Idiosyncratic romanization + English glosses** for all 64 hexagrams (see §5).
4. **Poetic two-layer oracle**: each hexagram gets a modern verse ORACLE, and each line gets a short verse + prose gloss.

### 1.8 Line-place semantics (places 1–6)
Reifler gives **no systematic place doctrine** (no "1 = beginning, 5 = ruler" schema). Place meaning is carried entirely by each line's verse oracle, which follows the traditional imagery (e.g. Hex 1: 1 "The dragon lies hidden in the deep. Take no action"; 2 "The dragon appears in the field. Confer with the great man"; 5 "The dragon wings through the sky"; 6 "The dragon overreaches. Guilt." — pp. 21–22). Lines are "numbered from bottom to top" (p. 11).

## 2. RULES (reading procedure + interpretive grammar)

**Casting rules**
- R1. Cast in solitude, in a spirit of religious acceptance, meditating on the question; "only if the sticks are cast in the spirit of the question will they indicate a hexagram that has meaning" (Intro).
- R2. Yarrow: 16-step procedure, repeated 6 times, lowest line first (pp. 8–9).
- R3. Coins: 3 coins × 6 tosses, bottom to top (p. 10).

**Moving-line rules (p. 11)**
- R4. Read the general oracle for the hexagram **plus** the oracles of the moving lines only.
- R5. "As long as you understand that only the moving line cast by you applies to you, there is no stricture against reading the oracles and interpretations of the other lines" — reading non-moving lines is allowed for clarification.
- R6. No moving lines → "the situation is either static or at an abrupt end and only the oracle for that particular hexagram is consulted."
- R7. Moving lines change to their opposites, producing a **second hexagram** that shows "how the present Tao… will change to another" (worked example: Hex 25 → Hex 24, moving lines 4, 5, 6).
- R8. All-six-moving special texts exist for Hexagrams 1 and 2: Hex 1 "A swarm of headless dragons. Auspicious." (six moving lines = "perfect balance", p. 22); Hex 2 "Keep to your course forever" (p. 26).

**Interpretive grammar (fixed per-hexagram format)**
- G1. Header: romanized name = English gloss; lower trigram / upper trigram named.
- G2. ORACLE: (a) an image-quatrain of the two trigrams ("Heaven in motion; the strength of the dragon"), (b) an action line about "the man" ("The man nerves himself for ceaseless activity"), (c) a verdict list ("Creative activity. / Influence. / Improvement. / Keep to your course." — the four-term formula yuan/heng/li/zhen appears verbatim only for Hexagrams 1 and 2).
- G3. INTERPRETATION in the fixed tripartite order **artha → kama → moksha**.
- G4. LINES 1→6, each: short verse oracle (often ending in a valence tag) + prose gloss addressed to "you".
- No "ruling line" doctrine; no judgment/image/line strata from the Chinese commentarial tradition (Reifler works from Legge's text but discards its structure).

## 3. SYNTAX / STRATA — formulaic phrase inventory (with valence)

Fixed valence morphemes used in verse oracles (counts from full text):
| Phrase | Count | Valence |
|---|---|---|
| Auspicious / Very auspicious | ~132 | + |
| Ominous | ~53 | − |
| No mistakes / No mistake | ~70 | neutral-positive (safe) |
| Guilt / No guilt / Guilt disappears | ~62 | − / resolving + |
| Keep to your course (perseverance formula) | ~93 | injunction (+ if followed) |
| You may cross the great water | 9 | + (go ahead, great undertaking) |
| Do not cross the great water | 1 | − injunction |
| Confer with the great man | 5 (+ "great man" 9 total) | + counsel |
| Take no action | 6 | neutral-caution |
| Success / Great success / No success | many | + / + / − |
| Misfortune | 16 | − |
| Danger, but no mistakes | recurring | mixed (risk + safety) |
| Peril | recurring | − |
| Regret(s) | ~32 | mild − |
| Good fortune | ~11 | + |
| Shame / Humiliation | 7 / 2 | − |
| Seek assistance / Carefully consider any advances / Advance / You may take any action you wish | verdict-list items | counsel |

Structural formula: ORACLE verdict lists = terse imperative/valence morphemes; LINES verse = image + valence tag; prose gloss = second-person psychological amplification. Reifler's distinctive strata choice: **the "superior man" becomes "the man" or "you"**; "great man" kept as "the great man" in oracles.

## 4. CORRESPONDENCE TABLES
- Trigram table (attributes/familial/animal/anatomical/element/color/season/direction) — transcribed in §1.4. This is the book's only systematic correspondence table.
- Hexagram reference chart (p. 17) is an image (8×8 upper×lower trigram grid); not transcribed.
- Recurring symbolic anchors inside texts: dragon = Yang creative force (Hex 1); mare = Yin responsive force (Hex 2); yellow = earth/modesty (Hex 2 line 5); southwest/northeast friend directions (Hex 2 oracle, from tradition).

## 6. CANDIDATE DIMENSION ATTRIBUTION (Movement/Evolution/Being/Design/Space)

| Fragment class | Proposed dimension | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Moving lines (6/9) | **Evolution** | "Moving lines indicate how the present Tao… will change to another" (p. 11) — pure becoming/temporality |
| Static hexagram (no moving lines) | **Being** (frozen state) | "the situation is either static or at an abrupt end" (p. 11) |
| Yin/Yang line types | **Being** (state quality) | "Yang represents the powers that direct and impel action. Yin represents action directly" (p. 23) |
| Trigram attributes | **Being** (qualities) | attribute lists are state/quality descriptors |
| Trigram directions/seasons | **Space / Evolution** | directions = Space; seasons = cyclical time (Evolution) |
| Trigram pair above/below (position) | **Design** | hexagram meaning "derives from the qualities of its trigrams and their related positions" (p. 13) — relational structure |
| Inner trigrams (2-3-4 / 3-4-5) | **Design** | hidden substructure of the figure (p. 16) |
| Hexagram as "Tao of the moment" | **Movement** | "indicates to the questioner his Tao, his natural direction" — a vector/where-to-go reading |
| artha / kama / moksha split | artha → **Movement** (action in society); kama → **Space** (relational container/resonance) [alt: Movement]; moksha → **Evolution** (liberation path) | definitions, p. 12 |
| ORACLE verdict morphemes (Auspicious/Ominous/Keep to your course) | **Movement** (vector valence: go/hold/turn) | they modulate the direction taken |
| Verdict "cross the great water" | **Movement** | threshold crossing, explicit motion |

## 7. Load-bearing quotes
- "The Yin/Yang principle represents the constant change and motion of the universe and thus of human experience" (p. 4).
- "the sixty-four hexagrams were formed into sixty-four examples of different ways of life, ways of being that covered the entire range of human experience" (Intro, ~pp. 4–5).
- "Most casts will reveal at least one moving line" (p. 11).
- "For purposes of simplicity and relevance the interpretation of each hexagram is divided into three sections… artha, kama and moksha" (p. 12).
- "Each of these eight trigrams was given a name and certain attributes were ascribed to it, relating to the position in the trigram of the Yin and Yang lines" (p. 13).

## Uncertainties
- OCR of trigram table 5th-attribute row incomplete (pp. 14–15).
- A few hexagram romanizations garbled by the scan (32, 42, 43, 55, 59 glosses marked [uncertain]).
- No explicit place-1..6 semantics; inferred only via traditional line imagery.
